title: Custom prompt — 8/4/2026
template: You are acting as: Expert Data Analyst.

title: Feature Spec Prompt
description: Turn a rough app idea into a complete, unambiguous build spec before you ask the AI to write any code.
bestPractices: Always get the spec confirmed before code generation starts — it's 10x cheaper to fix a spec than a finished build.
Name the exact UI states explicitly; 'error' and 'empty' are the two AI tools forget most often.
Keep one feature per spec prompt instead of the whole app at once.
example: Spec for a Pomodoro timer: user flow starts on Idle state, has Running/Paused/Break states, data model tracks {sessionsCompleted, currentDuration}, edge cases include tab close mid-session...

title: Debug & Fix Prompt
description: Get a targeted fix for broken code without triggering a full unwanted rewrite.

variables.label: Output format
options: Only the changed lines with context
variables.default: Only the changed lines with context

bestPractices: Paste the exact error text, not a paraphrase — exact wording often contains the real clue.
Explicitly say 'don't refactor unrelated code' to stop scope creep in the fix.
Ask for root cause explanation first so you actually learn the pattern, not just paste a fix.
example: Root cause: the loop mutates the array it's iterating over. Fix: iterate over a copy using [...array] instead of array directly.

title: UI/UX Design Brief Prompt
description: Brief the AI to design a premium, distinctive dark-themed interface instead of a generic template look.

variables.label: Must include
variables.default: responsive layout, hover states, empty states

bestPractices: Ask for the color/type reasoning before code — it forces a deliberate choice instead of a default.
Name a style direction explicitly; 'make it look nice' defaults to the same template every time.
Always request empty, loading, and error states in the same brief.
example: Palette: near-black #0B0F1A base, amber #F2A93B accent for actions, teal #4FD1C5 for secondary info — chosen to feel technical but warm, avoiding the common neon-on-black look.

title: System Prompt / API Integration Prompt
description: Get correct, working Claude API integration code inside a single-file HTML app.
template:
Add a Claude API integration to this single-file HTML app for: {{feature_purpose}}.

Requirements:
- Use fetch to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages
- Model: claude-sonnet-4-6, max_tokens: 1000
- Never include an API key in the code
- Input from user: {{input_source}}
- Expected output shape: {{output_shape}}
- Handle loading and error states in the UI

Return only the JS function plus the minimal UI hook needed, not the whole file.

variables.label: Input source
options: a textarea the user types into
the result of a previous API call
variables.default: a textarea the user types into

variables.label: Expected output shape
options: Structured JSON to render as UI
variables.default: Structured JSON to render as UI

bestPractices: Always explicitly forbid hardcoded API keys in the prompt.
Ask for loading/error UI states in the same request, not as an afterthought.
Request only the relevant function, not the whole file, to avoid it silently rewriting other parts.
example: async function callClaude(userInput) { const res = await fetch(...); const data = await res.json(); return data.content.map(b=>b.text).join(''); }

title: Structured Content Generator Prompt
description: Force clean, parseable JSON output for dynamic UI rendering instead of prose you have to clean up.
bestPractices: Explicitly say 'no markdown fences, no commentary' or the response will need cleanup before JSON.parse.
Tell it to use null instead of inventing data — this is the #1 cause of silently wrong structured output.
Give the exact schema with types, not a description in words.

title: Resume Bullet Rewriter
description: Turn a flat task description into an achievement-focused resume bullet with metrics.
bestPractices: Mark inferred metrics as [estimate] so you remember to verify before submitting.
Feed it one bullet at a time for higher quality than batching ten at once.
Always specify the target role — the same bullet reads differently for Analyst vs Engineer roles.
example: Built 5 interactive Power BI dashboards, cutting manual reporting time by an estimated 40% [estimate] across the internship team.

title: Cover Letter Generator
description: Generate a tailored, non-generic cover letter draft from a job description and your background.

variables.label: My background (2-3 lines)
variables.default: MCA graduate, 6 months Data Analyst internship, Python/SQL/Power BI

bestPractices: Paste the real job description, not a summary — specific phrases from it help the letter feel tailored.
Explicitly ban filler openers; this is the single biggest tell of an AI-written letter.
Always request a low-pressure call to action, not a demanding one.
example: Your posting's emphasis on 'turning raw data into stakeholder-ready dashboards' matches exactly what I did in my six months at PySpiders, where...

title: Job Posting Fit & Red-Flag Analyzer
description: Screen a job posting for mismatches, vague requirements, or red flags before you apply.
template:
Analyze this job posting for fit against my profile, and flag any red flags.

Job posting:
{{job_posting}}

My profile: {{my_profile}}

Output as:
1. Fit score (1-10) with reasoning
2. Red flags (vague titles, unrealistic requirement combos, unpaid trial work, salary omission, etc.)
3. 3 tailored questions I could ask in an interview to clarify ambiguity

variables.label: My profile summary
variables.default: MCA graduate, Data Analyst internship, targeting Data Analyst / Business Analyst / Python Developer roles

bestPractices: Always ask for a reasoned fit score, not just yes/no — the reasoning is what's actually useful.
Have it generate clarifying interview questions, not just flag problems, so you leave with next steps.
Re-run this on postings that feel 'too good' — vague scope is the most common red flag.
example: Fit score: 7/10. Red flag: '3-5 years experience' combined with 'entry-level salary' — scope mismatch worth clarifying.

title: Interview Prep Q&A Simulator
description: Practice likely interview questions for a specific role with structured feedback on your answers.
template: Act as an interviewer for a {{role}} position at a {{company_type}}. Ask me one question at a time from this category: {{question_category}}. After each answer I give, rate it 1-10 on structure and specificity, then give one concrete improvement before asking the next question.
bestPractices: Ask for one question at a time — batching questions kills the realism of interview practice.
Request a concrete improvement, not just a score, so each round actually compounds.
Rotate question categories across sessions instead of drilling only one type.
example: Q: Tell me about a time you found an error in a dataset. Feedback: 7/10 — good structure, add the quantified impact of catching it.

title: LinkedIn Post / Profile Optimizer
description: Improve a LinkedIn profile section or draft post for visibility and credibility without sounding generic.

variables.label: Goals
variables.default: get noticed by recruiters, sound specific not generic

bestPractices: Explicitly ban buzzwords — LinkedIn copy defaults to them heavily otherwise.
Anchor every claim to a real example so the output stays specific.
Match content type to intent: headline for search visibility, About for narrative.
example: Before: 'Passionate data professional.' After: 'I turn messy spreadsheets into Power BI dashboards leadership actually opens.'

title: EDA Kickoff Prompt
description: Get a structured exploratory data analysis plan for a new dataset before touching any code.
template:
I have a dataset: {{dataset_description}}.
Columns: {{columns}}
Goal of the analysis: {{analysis_goal}}

Give me an EDA plan with:
1. Data quality checks to run first (nulls, dtypes, duplicates, outliers)
2. 5 exploratory questions worth answering given the goal
3. Suggested chart type for each question
4. Any red flags to watch for given the column names above

Do not write code yet — plan first.
bestPractices: Always plan before coding — it prevents a wall of undirected pandas exploration.
List actual column names; generic prompts without them produce generic EDA plans.
Ask for red flags specifically — it catches issues like mixed types or suspicious constant columns early.
example: Q: Does fuel type correlate with region? Chart: grouped bar chart of fuel_type by region. Red flag: 'year' column stored as string.

title: SQL Query Generator from Plain English
description: Convert a plain-language data question into a correct, readable SQL query for your schema.
template:
Write a {{sql_dialect}} query for this question: {{question}}

Schema:
{{schema}}

Requirements:
- Use readable table aliases
- Add a one-line comment explaining any non-obvious join or subquery
- Optimize for readability over cleverness
bestPractices: Always paste the real schema — guessed column names is the #1 cause of wrong SQL.
Ask for comments on non-obvious joins so you can learn the pattern, not just copy it.
Specify the dialect; window functions and date handling differ a lot between engines.
example: SELECT c.customer_name, SUM(o.amount) AS total_spend FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.customer_name ORDER BY total_spend DESC;

title: Power BI Dashboard Design Brief
description: Plan a dashboard's layout, visuals, and DAX measures before opening Power BI.
template:
Design a Power BI dashboard for: {{dashboard_purpose}}.
Audience: {{audience}}
Available fields: {{fields}}

Give me:
1. Page layout (top KPIs, main visuals, filters panel)
2. Chart type for each key metric with reasoning
3. 3 DAX measures I'll likely need, with formulas
4. Filter/slicer recommendations
bestPractices: Specify the audience — an exec dashboard and an ops dashboard need very different density.
Ask for DAX formulas directly rather than just measure names, to save a build-test cycle.
Request layout structure (KPI row, filters panel) before picking individual charts.
example: KPI row: Total Revenue, YoY Growth %, Active Customers. DAX: YoY Growth % = DIVIDE([Revenue] - [Revenue LY], [Revenue LY])

title: Insight-to-Narrative Prompt
description: Turn raw analysis findings into a clear, stakeholder-ready narrative summary.
bestPractices: Force a single lead insight — reports that open with five findings bury the important one.
Cap recommendations at one; more reads as indecision to leadership audiences.
Match format to how it'll actually be consumed (email vs slide vs report).
example: The biggest driver of churn is support response time, not price — accounts with >24hr first response show 3x higher churn.

title: Data Cleaning Checklist Prompt
description: Get a systematic cleaning plan for a messy dataset, tailored to its actual quality issues.

variables.label: Known issues
variables.default: missing values, inconsistent date formats, duplicate rows

bestPractices: Ask for the reasoning behind step order — structural issues (dtypes, duplicates) should be fixed before value-level cleaning.
List known issues explicitly so the plan targets your actual data, not a generic checklist.
Specify the tool; pandas and Power Query solve the same problem very differently.
example: Step 1: standardize date formats (structural) before Step 4: impute missing values (value-level) — imputation on bad dtypes silently fails.
